messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: KV cache OOMs detected on hosted-runtime shard eu-west-1-a. Error rate spike and eviction flood. Priority: P1. Paging on-call.
anna-sre: ack, jumping in. Can someone paste the top log tail?
devon-runtime: pasting last 20s from runtime logs:
```
 2024-05-15T12:34:21Z runtime[svc]: session=abc123 seq=451 token_len=18000 prefetch_window=65536 kv_cache_alloc failed: out_of_memory
 2024-05-15T12:34:21Z runtime[svc]: session=def456 seq=780 token_len=24000 prefetch_window=65536 kv_cache_alloc failed: out_of_memory
 2024-05-15T12:34:22Z runtime[svc]: allocator: total_used=179GB total_free=1GB fallback=true
 2024-05-15T12:34:23Z runtime[svc]: evicting 1000 segments, reclaim=2MB -> evict loop
 2024-05-15T12:34:24Z runtime[svc]: continuous_batcher: window_size=512 -> batch growth to 2048 under long-context users
```
anna-sre: thanks. Looks like large token_len requests + prefetch exploded KV cache. Any recent config changes?
kai-mlinfra: yes — we flipped a batching/prefetch tweak in the hosted runtime prototype yesterday to increase prefetch_window and reduce cold-start overhead for long-context sessions. Flag: `enable_aggressive_prefetch=true` deployed at 11:10 UTC to eu-west-1.
raj-sre: that rings the bell. We saw higher throughput but didn't expect worst-case long prompts to multiply allocs.
emma-support: heads up — Support reporting degraded responses for 3 customers (2 paying enterprise, 1 high-traffic startup). They're seeing 504/timeouts when the runtime stalls. I've opened tickets and pinged the customer CS reps.
anna-sre: immediate mitigation plan: 1) rollback aggressive prefetch flag to false in eu-west-1; 2) apply short-term rate limit on requests > 12k tokens for hosted tier; 3) kick a runtime hotpatch to add defensive cap on kv prefetch per-session. Who can rollback the flag?
devon-runtime: I'll do the flag rollback and push a canary to a single AZ, then to the region. Rolling now: `feature-flagctl set enable_aggressive_prefetch=false --region eu-west-1`
ops-bot: Deploy started: feature-flagctl/2024-05-15T11:38 -> eu-west-1 (canary az: eu-west-1-b).
incident-bot: Handoff: @anna-sre is primary, @devon-runtime is executing mitigations.
kai-mlinfra: also recommend temporarily lowering `continuous_batcher.window_limit` to 256 to avoid batch growth. I'll prepare the flag.
devon-runtime: lowered window_limit to 256 via runtime config service. `PATCH /runtime-configs/eu-west-1 {"continuous_batcher.window_limit": 256}` -> applied.
anna-sre: good. raj, can you watch memory graphs and eviction rate?
raj-sre: watching. Dashboard: memory used per-host dropping from 95% -> 60% within 2 minutes after rollback started. Eviction loop rate decreasing.
emma-support: customer-impact update: Enterprise A (acct ent-114) reported 37 failing requests in last 30m, response times > 30s. I've escalated and shared workaround (reduce prompt size). They're asking for root cause ETA.
anna-sre: root cause: aggressive prefetch + continuous batching allowed many long-context sessions to prefill huge KV windows which multiplied memory usage; led to evict loops and OOMs. Short-term mitigation done. Next steps: triage and permanent fix.
devon-runtime: confirmed runtime clusters back to healthy: p95 latency normalized, error rate back to baseline. Rolling rollback to remaining AZs now.
ops-bot: feature-flagctl completed: enable_aggressive_prefetch=false -> eu-west-1 (all AZs).
kai-mlinfra: for permanent fix I propose: - add per-session prefetch budget (cap tokens prefetched to 8k) - add a throttled backpressure path for continuous_batcher that refuses to grow beyond safe region-level memory threshold - automated rollback if eviction_rate > X
anna-sre: sounds good. Let's create a short-lived mitigation RFC and assign owners.
anna-sre: @kai-mlinfra you own design, @devon-runtime you own rollout plan and automated rollback, @raj-sre you own alert thresholds for eviction_rate and memory pressure. ETA for RFC?
kai-mlinfra: I'll draft RFC in the infra repo within 24h.
devon-runtime: will add rollback hook and unit tests, aiming for a hotfix release tomorrow morning UTC.
raj-sre: I'll tune alerts and add a paging rule to fire earlier when eviction_rate spikes > 50/min.
emma-support: customer comms: I'll send status update to impacted customers with timeline and mitigation steps. Mentioned we have reduced risk and rolled back flag.
anna-sre: postmortem actions: - postmortem doc (owner: anna-sre) - add regression test in canary harness to simulate many long-token sessions to validate prefetching heuristics - add billing/monitoring per-session token distribution to detect heavy long-context users - evaluate whether hosted tier needs per-request token soft-limits
devon-runtime: note: there is a small risk of recurrence if a single user sends repeated 40k token prompts; we'll add a hard cap in the runtime config for now: `max_prefetch_tokens_per_session=8192`
ops-bot: Runtime hotpatch deployed: runtime/2024-05-15T12:45 -> eu-west-1 (patch: cap prefetch).
raj-sre: memory stabilized across hosts. No new OOMs in last 10 minutes.
anna-sre: excellent. Closing immediate pager. Leave thread open for follow-ups.
emma-support: I'll confirm with the three impacted customers that service is back to normal and post an update in customer tickets.
kai-mlinfra: one more note: add canary traffic profile for 'long_prompts' to our chaos suite so this doesn't slip past next time.
anna-sre: agreed. I'll own the postmortem and link this thread. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident resolved: KV cache OOMs — mitigated by flag rollback and runtime cap. Severity downgraded to P2. Logs and postmortem: link to /incidents/1719008888/postmortem (placeholder).
